thesis_quotes: Churn is driven by misrouting + expectation mismatch, not sensorial failure.
Sensorials are not driving churn. They hold even when users exit the category.
Shelf life is a habit suppressant more than a direct reject reason.
Prioritise removal of refrigeration to encourage intended usage frequency & habit formation.

variant_performance.notes: Biggest volume + biggest issue driver: redness/irritation/dryness on dry/sensitive/combo skin; weak pigmentation efficacy (2/8 improved); runny texture; quantity complaints.
Gentle, fine-hair-reduction win; ineffective for pigmentation; runny over time.
Balanced, low irritation; early pouch-packaging complaints.
Clear acne control for oily skin; dryness for dry/sensitive skin.
100% churn — not travel-friendly, seasonal-only effectiveness, poorest value perception.

usage_reality.headline: 56% scrub twice weekly | 30% scrub once weekly | 74% use Mura alone (no facewash pairing)
usage_reality.shelf_life_finding: Intended '2 months + refrigeration' vs Observed: users store in fridge, save Mura for occasions, and some discard it on suspected spoilage. Shelf life functions as a habit suppressant more than a direct reject reason.

churn_drivers_ranked.label: Cinnamon Nashpati misrouting to dry/sensitive/combo skin
Low-frequency use + short shelf life -> expiry -> poor value perception

geo_notes.note: 100% churn (3/3) — dry climate × sensitive skin × harshness.
Higher continued usage despite dryness complaints — climate tolerance, not just skin type.
Polarised — high trial volume, high satisfaction AND high churn; needs variant gating.
Higher tolerance, high sensorial scores, fewest adverse reactions — flagged as the safest test market for a new format.

cohort_summaries.name: Active Loyalist
cohort_summaries.headline: Stay due to habit, trust, and better performance than other natural brands — but hydration is a clear weak spot.
cohort_summaries.quote: Active loyalists stay due to habit, trust, and better performance than other natural brands. However, hydration is a clear weak spot — the key opportunity is improving benefit communication and variant tolerance before performance-led competitors become a stronger pull.
cohort_summaries.action: Protect this base with better hydration communication and variant-fit guidance; don't let performance-led challengers win them on predictability.

cohort_summaries.name: Active Trialist
cohort_summaries.headline: Like the cleansing, not yet convinced on pigmentation results; texture and mild CN irritation deter repeat purchase.
cohort_summaries.quote: Trialists like the cleaning, but are not fully convinced on pigmentation results. Texture issues and slight irritation (CN) are deterring the trialists from purchasing at least 3 packs in 6 months.
cohort_summaries.action: Convert with clearer benefit communication, better skin-comfort formulation, and stronger pack-size value perception.

cohort_summaries.name: Active User
cohort_summaries.headline: CN drives both usage and discontinuation — people move to it for pigmentation, then leave the category from rashes/ineffectiveness.
cohort_summaries.quote: People did move to Cinnamon Nashpati for pigmentation correction, but its ineffectiveness/rashes make it worse than the rest of the category — turning 3 active users into full lapsers.
cohort_summaries.action: Route pigmentation-seekers away from CN into a reformulated / better-tolerated option; fix the value-communication gap on pack size.

cohort_summaries.name: Lapser
cohort_summaries.headline: Did not lapse over price — lapsed over product issues, led by drying/harshness.
cohort_summaries.quote: Lapsers did not lapse because of price/qty perception, but because of product issues — drying (40%), followed by ineffectiveness. The non-negotiable for the category is non-drying exfoliation.
cohort_summaries.action: Treat non-drying exfoliation as a hard formulation requirement for the new range, not a nice-to-have.

cohort_summaries.name: Loyal Lapser
cohort_summaries.headline: Still like the product (7.9 for the true lapsers, ex-repeat-buyers even higher) — lapsed from inconvenience and unmet efficacy, not dislike.
cohort_summaries.quote: Lapsing is ineffectiveness-led, followed by inconvenience (low shelf life / price-qty), and a couple of occasional/gifting purchases with no intent to form a habit.
cohort_summaries.action: A shelf-stable, always-ready format directly targets this group's stated 'cumbersome to use in time' friction.

recommendations: Remove the refrigeration requirement to unlock intended daily/frequent-use habit formation (P1).
Reformat/re-pack for a daily-use claim — larger formats or stabilized, non-perishable preservative systems (P2).
Fix Cinnamon Nashpati's routing problem — gate dry/sensitive skin away from it at point of sale, or reformulate for broader tolerance; could lift NPS to 8.7-8.8 for natural-seeker segments.
Make non-drying exfoliation a non-negotiable formulation requirement, not a nice-to-have.
Reset expectations for concern-solving — communicate scrub as a maintenance/exfoliation + glow product, not a guaranteed pigmentation/acne corrector.
Address quantity/value perception with bigger packs or clearer value framing relative to shelf life and frequency.
Move now, while the category still reads as 'naturals-only' — before derm/clinical entrants and challenger natural brands capture pigmentation/acne seekers.

market_landscape.source_note: Amazon/Flipkart/Nykaa/Myntra/Quick-commerce category landscape, Helium 10 + keyword data, Jan 2026 — 75 ASINs, 111,914 units, ₹7.74 Cr category revenue analyzed on Amazon alone.

top_asins.product: Coffee Tan & Dead Skin Removal Scrub

price_quantity.note: Driven by Niconi & ClayCo — premium pricing, minimal price resistance (5-10% of reviews mention price).

packaging_format.note: 11 of 17 jar SKUs belong to Dr. Rashel.

trend_enzyme_ahabha.headline: Enzyme / AHA-BHA scrubs are the live trend, displacing grainy physical exfoliants
trend_enzyme_ahabha.detail: Consumers are moving away from harsh, grainy physical scrubs toward gentler, science-based exfoliation. ClayCo (21% ingredient-level share) and Suroskie lead this trend; both rank at the top of Amazon 'face scrub' search (ClayCo tagged Best Seller). ClayCo's Amazon search volume: 32,000/month; P/Q Rs 10.5/g.

trend_powder_whitespace.headline: Powder-format microfoliant is a genuine white space — and the one format in this research that plausibly solves refrigeration
trend_powder_whitespace.detail: Dermalogica-style powder microfoliants (Papaya enzyme, AHA/BHA, Hyaluronic acid, Oatmeal, Coconut Oil) sell at Rs 4,600-5,200 (P/Q Rs 62-70/g) and are Nykaa bestsellers, tagged 'Derm Approved' on Tira — with zero direct format competitors identified in this dataset. Powder inherently avoids the water-activity/preservation problem of wet cream scrubs, though the research doesn't say so explicitly. Distribution is currently Nykaa/Tira-only, absent from Amazon — a possible discovery gap, not a demand gap.

ingredient_trends.note: Most-used, least premium — saturated physical exfoliant.
Common brightening actives with NO brand owning major share — a stated white space.

review_voice_of_customer.headline: Irritation/burning/redness on sensitive or dry skin is the single most consistent negative theme across every reviewed brand and price tier, regardless of format.

so_what: The category is a two-brand oligopoly by revenue: Niconi (60.3%) + ClayCo (20.4%) = ~81% of Amazon face-scrub revenue from 2 SKUs.
Premium pricing is not being punished — perceived value stays strong even at Rs 1,300-1,400, provided efficacy/positioning is credible.
'Natural' positioning is over-crowded and under-monetized: 44% of brands, only 7.2% of revenue. Natural-only claims are not a differentiator on their own.
Brightening actives (Vitamin C, Niacinamide) are a white space — talked about by 42% of new-age brands, owned by none.
Physical/walnut exfoliation is saturated and commoditized; the live trend is enzyme/AHA-BHA (gentler, science-led).
Tan removal — not 'exfoliation' generically — is the dominant search and purchase driver (100% of generic search volume, 65% of branded search).
Combo economics work: bundling drives outsized share of brand revenue (e.g. Mamaearth's face+scrub combo = 50% of its category revenue).
Powder format is a credible, currently-uncontested white space that structurally sidesteps the refrigeration problem — at a premium price ceiling.

niconi_deep_dive.headline: Niconi is a single-SKU, 60.3%-of-category-revenue oligopolist — and it got there by refusing to compete on price, naturals, or legacy trust.

strategy_pillars.detail: Niconi and ClayCo are the only two SKUs in the ₹1300-1400 band — just 2 SKUs, 46% of category volume, but 81% of category revenue. Driven by Niconi & ClayCo — premium pricing, minimal price resistance (5-10% of reviews mention price).

strategy_pillars.pillar: A packaging moat, not a tube
strategy_pillars.detail: 58.5% of all face-scrub SKUs ship in a plain tube, worth only 36.0% of revenue. Niconi instead owns the Bottle/Dispenser format almost outright (Almost entirely Niconi's dispenser bottle.) — just 5 products, yet 60.7% of category revenue. The format itself signals 'treatment', not 'scrub'.

strategy_pillars.pillar: One hero ingredient, not a natural-ingredients list
strategy_pillars.detail: Kojic Acid appears in only 2 brands' SKUs (Niconi + ClayCo's glycolic-acid analog) but drives 60.7% of category revenue from 30.6% of volume. Niconi-driven; premium brightening active. Contrast: 33 brands compete on 'Natural' positioning (the largest brand count of any segment) yet capture only 7.2% of revenue between them — naturals is a crowded, low-power claim; one named premium active is not.

strategy_pillars.pillar: Reframed the job: tan/brightening treatment, not exfoliation commodity
strategy_pillars.detail: The hero SKU name is literally 'Tan Vanish Gluta-Kojic Skin Polish' — sold as a targeted skin-tone treatment at ₹7.7/g, roughly 6.4x the ₹100-200 commodity band's typical rate. It converts a modest 30.0% volume share into 60.3% revenue share — proof buyers will pay a premium once the product is framed as solving a specific concern rather than as a generic scrub.

niconi_deep_dive.implication_for_nat_habit: Nat Habit's current Mura combo SKU sells at ₹184 for 25g (₹3.7/g) — inside the crowded, low-margin ₹100-200 tube band, competing on the same 'natural ingredients' claim as 32 other brands for 7.2% of category revenue. Niconi's playbook says the premium is unlocked by combining three things at once: a distinct format (not a tube), one named hero active with a specific promise, and a confident price that matches that promise — not by naturalness alone. This is the single biggest strategic input the market landscape offers for the new range's pricing and packaging decisions.

new_range_case.problem_statement: Nat Habit's current Mura face scrub has a ~2-month shelf life and needs refrigeration — a format that suppresses the very daily/weekly habit it's designed to build, is hard to manufacture and ship at scale, and (per the cohort study) makes users ration, forget, or discard product rather than use it as intended.
non_negotiables: No refrigeration requirement — removes the #1 cited habit suppressant.
Non-drying exfoliation — the single most-repeated 'must fix' across both the new survey and the existing-user cohort study.
Retain the natural-ingredient trust Nat Habit already owns (80%+ of Mura users cite it as a reason to trial/repeat) — don't trade it away chasing a clinical-actives story wholesale.
Fix Cinnamon Nashpati-style skin-type misrouting — either via reformulation for broader tolerance or clearer at-purchase guidance.

format_options.format: Reformulated cream/gel with stabilized preservative system
format_options.pros: Closest to current sensorial experience; least R&D risk; keeps Cinnamon-Nashpati-style variants viable if reformulated for tolerance.
format_options.cons: Most crowded format (Tube=58.5% of category volume but only 36% of revenue) — hardest to stand out on shelf.

format_options.pros: Rides the one live trend in the category (ClayCo, Suroskie); addresses the #1 VoC complaint (irritation) better than grit-based exfoliation; still liquid/gel, familiar to shoppers.
format_options.cons: Needs credible active-ingredient sourcing/story; category leader (ClayCo) already owns 21% ingredient share — needs real differentiation, not a me-too.

format_options.format: Powder-based microfoliant (activate with water at use)
format_options.pros: Structurally solves the refrigeration/shelf-life problem outright (no free water = no spoilage risk); zero direct competitors found in this research; premium positioning headroom (Rs 62-70/g benchmark).
format_options.cons: Unfamiliar format for Indian face-scrub shoppers — needs usage education; currently proven only at a very high price point, may need a mass-accessible SKU too; distribution gap (Nykaa/Tira only, not Amazon) to solve for, not copy.

format_options.pros: No refrigeration, travel-friendly (directly answers the Five Gram Mura '0% retention, not travel-friendly' failure), low-preservative by nature.
format_options.cons: Zero comparable products found in this category's research — genuinely unproven for face scrubs in this market; sensorial experience furthest from what current Mura users are used to.

pricing_recommendation.headline: Price the new range at Rs 200-299 for a 1-month supply, with room to test a Rs 300+ 'hero' SKU.
pricing_recommendation.rationale: 64.4% of new-survey respondents are comfortable at Rs 150-249; 62.7% at Rs 200+. Category data shows minimal price resistance even at premium tiers (Niconi/ClayCo at Rs 1,300+ face <10% price complaints in reviews) provided efficacy is credible — so Nat Habit is very likely under-pricing relative to what its own natural-trust positioning could support, once the format problem is solved.

new_range_case.positioning_recommendation: Lead with 'fresh, natural ingredients with visible exfoliation and glow, without the fridge' — 89.8% of survey respondents said they'd definitely/probably buy a Nat Habit scrub on that promise alone (non-users were slightly MORE bullish than existing users, 94.1% vs 88.1% — this is a broad-appeal reformulation story, not a niche one). Communicate scrub as a maintenance/glow/texture product, not a guaranteed pigmentation or acne corrector, to avoid the 'expectation mismatch' churn the cohort study flags.
next_steps: Shortlist 1-2 shelf-stable formats (enzyme/AHA-BHA gel is the lowest-risk pick; powder is the highest-upside/highest-education-cost pick) for formulation trials against the non-drying requirement.
Re-gate Cinnamon-Nashpati-style variants away from dry/sensitive skin at point of sale, or reformulate for broader tolerance, independent of the shelf-life fix.
Pilot the new format in East India (Kolkata/WB) first, per the cohort study's climate-tolerance finding, before a national rollout.
Re-test pricing at Rs 250-299 once the shelf-stable reformulation is ready — the category shows this is defensible if efficacy is credible.

Design pack size around the actual observed use rate (56% twice-weekly, 30% weekly) rather than the aspirational daily claim, to fix the 'quantity feels insufficient' perception that hits even satisfied users.
